extracted.intended_audience: professional researchers seeking funding from the Alzheimer's Association International Research Grant Program
extracted.subtask_description: Information and expectations for researchers applying to the Alzheimer's Association International Research Grant Program (IRGP), including program focus, eligibility, application process, and review governance. Targets investigators preparing grant applications or seeking program-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus — research aims to advance understanding and care
rubrics_metrics.description: The Alzheimer's Association International Research Grant Program (IRGP) funds investigations to advance our understanding of Alzheimer's disease, identify new treatment strategies, improve care for people with dementia and further our knowledge of brain health and disease prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should align with one or more of these high-level aims. The program funds a wide range of projects from basic discovery science to studies addressing social and behavioral aspects of Alzheimer's and related dementias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research supported — broad portfolio across disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grant program supports investigators at every professional stage and includes categories designed to address gaps in research efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can propose work across the translational spectrum (basic to social/behavioral). Consider whether the proposed study addresses an identified gap in the existing research portfolio or fits a specific grant category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — investigators at every professional stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Research Program supports investigators at every professional stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program includes multiple categories to accommodate different career stages; applicants should select the category appropriate for their professional stage and career development needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic eligibility — U.S. and international researchers eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our grants are open to U.S. and international researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from outside the U.S. may apply; review any individual funding opportunity announcements for additional location- or institution-specific eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process and deadlines — follow posted procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about our grant application process and key deadlines. View and Apply for a Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the program's application instructions and meet published deadlines. Use the 'How to Apply' and specific grant posting pages to obtain submission requirements, forms, and timeline details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funded studies database — review past funded abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Search Our Funded Studies: View abstracts of studies supported by our research funding. You can also search for specific dementia grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the funded studies database to understand prior awards, avoid redundancy, and position proposals to fill unmet needs or gaps in the portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program governance and review support — IRGP Council role
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRGP Council assists with crafting requests for grant applications, provides expertise during the review process and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that RFAs and review processes are informed by the IRGP Council; review criteria, priorities, or emphasis areas may reflect Council input. Contact program staff or consult RFAs for specific review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and inquiries — use provided program contact
rubrics_metrics.description: For more information about our grants projects, or if you have questions about a specific grant, please email grantsapp@alz.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct application-specific or eligibility questions to the grants team prior to submission to clarify requirements or seek guidance on fit.
